name: sector-etf/sector-sleeve-blend
title: Sector sleeve blend — overnight reversal + flow calendar + RSI(2) dips + rate rotation
description: Four weak, nearly uncorrelated edges on the 11 SPDR sector ETFs + SPY, each risk-scaled once a year from its own expanding vol: long/short sectors against their recent overnight returns (SPY beta-hedged), an equal-weight sector basket in turn-of-month / pre-FOMC / pre-holiday windows, Connors RSI(2) dip buys above the 200-day SMA, and a sector rate-beta × 10y-yield-trend rotation. Gross capped at 2.0.
direction: long/short basket, net long on average (+0.36; range -0.38 to +2.0)

backtest.cost_type: all-in (spread + fee), charged on sum|dw|; returns in excess of T-bills on net dollar exposure

live_notes: SIM book: filled at the yfinance daily close from the shared data/ cache, with no order book, rejection or partial fill. Weaker evidence than a venue fill -- do not read this track as exchange-cleared. The book also charges no margin interest on days net long exceeds 1 and pays none on idle cash, so compare the live curve with the TOTAL-RETURN Sharpe (0.94 / 0.89 OOS), not the T-bill-excess headline.

Cost: broker set to 1 bp slippage + 1 bp fee = the research's 2 bp/side all-in. Report ladder: 0 bp -> 0.98, 2 bp -> 0.88, 5 bp -> 0.73 (0.65 OOS). NOTE: live_lib.broker_from_meta (the dashboard's flatten button) rebuilds a basket with the 1 bp / 10 bp defaults = 11 bp/side; that affects a one-off flatten only, not the daemon.

Borderline and says so: below Sharpe 1 OOS (0.81), and sleeve choice plus the yearly weighting scheme were picked after seeing results. The selection-free WF7 control gives 0.62 OOS; the report's honest forward expectation is Sharpe 0.6-0.8. OOS alpha vs SPY 5.4 %/yr, t 1.97. The case is diversification (beta 0.26, rho ~0 with treasury-flow-calendar and crypto-alts BAB).

Gross cap: deployed at the tested spec, 2.0 (binds ~1 % of days). JUMP RISK: worst days -10.0 % (2011-08-08), -8.8 % (2020-02-27), -5.7 % (2018-02-05) against a 1 % VaR of -1.9 %, from the DIP sleeve buying into crash legs. The report offers gross_cap=1.0 (same Sharpe 0.88 / 0.85 OOS, worst day -5.7 %, CAGR 7.1 %) as an option examined after the spec was fixed -- not deployed; switching would restart the book.

History: the yearly sleeve risk weights use each sleeve's expanding vol from its first trade (1999-2002), so the runner loads the full 1998+ panel via code/sector-etf/shared/data.load_panel, which splices data/<T>_d_pre2010.parquet onto the live cache. If those pre-2010 files disappear the runner refuses to trade (MIN_BARS 6500) rather than run on different weights.

10y yield: ^TNX from yfinance (spliced with IDX_TNX_d_pre2010.parquet), as the spec directs for live use; the headline used FRED DGS10. Research tnx_check: 0.89 full / 0.84 OOS, daily rho 0.996. On the deploy bar the two yields move the weights by up to 0.034 per leg.

Calendar upkeep: code/sector-etf/sector-sleeve-blend/fomc_dates.csv runs through 2027 -- append the next year's Fed schedule each December (the runner logs a warning within 90 days of its end). NYSE holidays for day t+1 come from rules in strategy.py; unscheduled closures (9/11, state funerals, Sandy) are not known in advance.

Timing: row t of target_weights is held close_t -> close_{t+1} and uses Open_t as well as Close_t. The daemon wakes 00:00:20 UTC and trades only when the bar all 12 legs agree on changes; a re-check during US hours that pulls a forming bar raises instead of trading it, and any leg lagging SPY's bar blocks the rebalance.

Deploy check 2026-09-25: runner --check on bar 2026-09-24 equals target_weights(close, open_, y10=^TNX) recomputed over the same panel exactly (gross 1.357, net +0.404; largest legs XLE +0.32, XLB -0.16, SPY +0.16, XLF +0.15). backtest_series.parquet stores RETURNS, not weights; the recomputed DGS10 book's net returns match it at lag 0 (max|diff| 2.5e-4, mean 1.6e-7, rho 0.9999999) and reproduce Sharpe 0.880 / 0.941 / 0.809.
